**GREEN 2026-08-21 (cc), AND EVERYTHING FROM `STILL RED` ONWARDS IS RETAINED AS HISTORY RATHER THAN AS STATE.** Read the paragraphs below as the record of why this row was red for three days, not as a description of today. Three of their claims are now false and are corrected here rather than silently: (1) `STILL RED` -- the row is green; (2) `nothing gates on it` -- dc wired it at `5d2b1f0d`, three call sites, dispatched UNCONDITIONALLY; (3) `Whoever admits it wants the path trigger` -- **hv RULED AGAINST the path trigger this session**, taking the unconditional form at a measured cost of roughly 4.6s -> 7.3s on the gate total, so the row's own recommendation is superseded by a later ruling and a builder following it would now be going against hv. **THE BLOCKER THIS ROW RECORDED IS DISCHARGED: the `--staged` mode cc's revert demanded now exists** -- `canon_commit_check.sh:254` parses the flag and clears `REV`, `:364` asks `git diff-index --cached HEAD`, and the file is 464 lines against the 425 cc measured. **EVIDENCE FOR THE GREEN, DRIVEN BY cc RATHER THAN TAKEN FROM THE BUILDER, AND dc DECLINED TO CERTIFY THEIR OWN WIRING WHICH IS WHY THIS WAS cc's TO MOVE.** The property is SYMMETRIC and both directions were witnessed: **canon ahead of the commit** -- cc's own commit refused at `ADDS 1 of 89`, UNPLANTED, when a thread-scoped sync ingested a peer's untracked file; and **the file ahead of canon** -- a tracked attachment edited and staged alone, refused at `ADDS 1 of 1` naming `stale_at_check.sh`, driven in a detached worktree. **The negative control is cc's own next commit at `ADDS 0`, rc=0, after sync-then-commit-together** -- so the refusal is attributable to the divergence and not to the gate refusing everything. **And the inherited-breakage clause the criterion calls load-bearing is BUILT rather than assumed**: the tool prints `INHERITED -- NOT EXAMINED in narrowed mode, and this is structural rather than an omission`, which is the 23-of-46 problem the criterion's own text says would otherwise make this a gate nobody keeps. **Where cc's 2026-08-19 planted index divergence printed `EXAMINED 0 of 280` at exit 0, the wired form examined 88 and refused** -- the pending commit is no longer invisible to it. Two unplanted catches, two owners, one afternoon. **COST FIGURES ARE THREE AND NONE ARE COMPARABLE**, which is the roster's own warning applied here: cc 3.6-4.9s at `61b93440`, dc 2710-2760ms narrowed at `ecea0eeb`, and 2.49-2.55s recorded at `4ba598f1` -- different revisions and machines, so each is stated with its subject and none is subtracted from another. **WHAT THIS GREEN DOES NOT CLAIM**, per the criterion's own three-way split: a green at HEAD is NARROWED and EXHAUSTIVE-at-a-revision at best, and neither establishes the property itself, which is a claim about EVERY commit. A gate cannot repair the past and this row does not pretend to. --- HISTORY FOLLOWS --- **STILL RED, AND FOR A DEEPER REASON THAN THIS ROW RECORDS -- cc BUILT THE WIRING, MEASURED IT, AND REVERTED IT (2026-08-19).** The row says the instrument is built and the criterion is unmet because nothing gates on it. **True, and NOT the blocker.** cc wired it end to end -- `G_CANONCOMMIT`, `--list-guards`, a path-triggered call site, roster moved to `gated` -- and `runner_roster_check.sh` went GREEN at 11 gated / 6 manual. **Then the positive control disagreed with every instrument that watches this.** **`canon_commit_check.sh` TAKES A COMMITTED REVISION: `REV="HEAD"` by default, comparing `$REV` against `$REV^`. There is no index mode -- vc confirmed by reading: no `--cached`, no `git show :`, no `diff-index` anywhere in its 425 lines.** **AT PRE-COMMIT TIME HEAD IS THE PARENT OF THE COMMIT BEING MADE, so the gate evaluates what the PREVIOUS commit added.** cc measured both directions: a divergence planted IN THE INDEX in an isolated worktree printed `EXAMINED 0 of 280` at exit 0 -- **the pending commit is invisible to it** -- while the same tool at `d980e5b5`, one of the five episode commits, printed `ADDS 3 of 275` at exit 1. **It works perfectly, on revisions that already exist.** **SO GATING IT AT ITS DEFAULT IS WORSE THAN NOT GATING IT, IN BOTH DIRECTIONS AT ONCE: the harmful commit sails through because while it is being made the tool is looking at its parent, AND THE NEXT COMMIT IS BLOCKED FOR ITS PARENT'S FAULT** -- which is precisely blocking on inherited breakage, the failure this criterion's own text names as what turns a gate into one nobody keeps. dc's 23-of-46 measurement is the argument and this wiring delivers exactly the 23 version. **WHAT IT NEEDS IS A `--staged` MODE, NOT A CALL SITE: the criterion is _a commit must not contain canon naming bytes not in that same commit_, and at pre-commit time THAT SAME COMMIT IS THE INDEX.** `git show :<path>` and `git diff-index --cached` are the index-side equivalents of what the tool already does with `git show $REV:<path>` and `git diff-tree`. A real change to a 425-line instrument rather than a flag. **AND THE ROSTER'S REASON FOR HOLDING IT `manual` HAS EXPIRED, KILLED BY AN UNRELATED COMMIT: it read _there is no narrow attachment-sync verb ... revisit after ST0057 WP-08_, and `sync --to-store <ID>` landed at `212b0075` this morning.** Every node can now sync one thread without ingesting the board. **Nothing pointed at that row when the verb landed and nothing could have -- a recorded reason true when written, made false elsewhere, with no instrument watching the join.** cc found it by reading the row they had to touch. **Re-measured while there: 3.6-4.9s at `61b93440` against 2.49-2.55s recorded at `4ba598f1` -- the estate grew and the figure did not follow, so it is now the SLOWEST instrument in the gate.** Whoever admits it wants the path trigger.

**IT FIRED UNPLANTED, ON A REAL COMMIT, 2026-08-20 -- AND THAT IS STRONGER EVIDENCE THAN ANY PLANTED CONTROL.** cc committed `1e2bc65e` (the gate arm itself) with an edited attachment and canon still naming the old bytes. Verified by vc at zero hops rather than carried: `canon_commit_check.sh 1e2bc65e` -> **rc=1, ADDS 1 of 1 examined**; the two repair commits `aa4c3ac0` and `9e191824` -> rc=0. **A planted divergence proves the mechanism works; an unplanted one proves the condition is REACHABLE by a careful node on an ordinary day.** This row now has both.

**AND IT CONFIRMS THIS NOTE'S OWN DIAGNOSIS RATHER THAN AMENDING IT: the tool caught it AFTER the fact, because it reads a committed revision.** `1e2bc65e` is **permanently divergent in history** -- the repair fixes the next commit and can never reach that one. **That is the cost of `manual`, measured in a lost commit rather than argued.**

**dc's FRAMING IS THE ONE THAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS NOT ABOUT THE NODE: _a control which depends on the author remembering is not a control, it is a hope with a filename._** cc wrote it up as their own carelessness; dc refused the harsher reading and applied their own guard-roster sentence unchanged. **The instrument is rostered `manual`, nothing dispatches it, so nothing did.** cc is the second node to hit this exact file class, with the rule in bold on their own board -- which is the evidence that remembering does not scale, not that anyone was careless.

**THIRD MEMBER OF A CLASS THIS ESTATE NOW HAS THREE OF, AND IT SHOULD BE READ AS A CLASS: an instrument that is BUILT, CORRECT, ROSTERED, AND DISPATCHED BY NOTHING.** `canon-ignore-guard.sh` (rostered in `pre-commit.sh`, whose roster this repo's commit path never reads -- AT-01.5); `append-only-guard.sh` (same roster, same silence, and it is the alarm on `intent/events.jsonl` -- AC-09.2); and this one (`manual`, which names no dispatcher at all). **Three instruments, three dispositions, one outcome.** `manual` is not a lighter form of `gated` -- **it is a disposition whose enforcement is a person's memory, and it cost a permanently divergent commit on the day it was tested.**

**BOTH RECORDED BLOCKERS LANDED, AND ONLY ONE OF THEM IS VERIFIED (cc 2026-08-20, measured at `e79991fc`; vc recording the distinction).** The roster's reason -- _no narrow attachment-sync verb, revisit after WP-08_ -- died at `212b0075`, and this note already carried that. **The second one, _what it needs is a `--staged` MODE, not a call site_, died at `19268867`.** So the row now reads as blocked on two things that both exist. **THE MODE EXISTING IS NOT THE MODE FIRING: cc is driving whether `--staged` actually catches an index-side divergence, and admission waits on that measurement rather than on the mode's presence** -- admitting it before would deliver a gate that examines nothing, which is the `EXAMINED 0 of 280` result this note already records from the default mode. **Second time in one day that `sync --to-store <ID>` has retired a recorded blocker nobody was watching; the first was AC-08.5's third burning case, which vc had written and vc refuted the same morning.**

**THE MEASUREMENT ADMISSION WAS WAITING ON IS DONE, AND `--staged` FIRES (cc, 2026-08-20 at `f585f848`, five arms, every one paired).** Positive: divergence STAGED under `--staged` -> `EXAMINED 1 of 286`, `ADDS 1 of 1`, rc=1. Pair 1: the same edit UNSTAGED -> examined 0, rc=0. **Pair 2 is the argument for the flag in one line -- the same tree with the same staged divergence, run in the DEFAULT mode, sees nothing** -- which is this note's own diagnosis measured rather than argued. Inherited: a divergent HEAD does not block an unrelated commit (rc=0), and `--exhaustive` on that same tree reports `INHERITED 191 of 286`, **so _excluded_ means excluded rather than invisible -- the clause that makes the narrowing safe rather than merely quiet.** **BOTH RECORDED BLOCKERS ARE NOW DEAD AND BOTH ARE VERIFIED. Nothing in this row waits on a measurement any more; admission is dc's.**

**ONE NUMBER RECORDED WITH ITS LIMIT STATED, BECAUSE IT IS ESTATE-SCALE AND NOBODY IS CHASING IT: `INHERITED 191 of 286` is 190 pre-existing plus cc's planted one. TWO THIRDS OF RECORDED ATTACHMENTS NAME BYTES THEIR OWN COMMIT DOES NOT HOLD.** Consistent with dc's 23-of-46 on a different denominator. **Not verified individually and no claim is made about causes.** What it supports is exactly one thing: **the gate must be ADDS-only**, because a gate that refused on the inherited two thirds is one nobody would keep -- which is the inherited-breakage argument this criterion's own text already makes, now with a number behind it.

**THE DELIVERABLE THIS ROW ASKS FOR ALREADY EXISTS, IS CORRECT, AND IS DISPATCHED BY NOTHING (cc found it 2026-08-20; vc drove it 16:45Z).** `intent/st/ST0056/parity/tools/canon_commit_check.sh`, 27783 bytes, written by dc on 2026-08-19. Driven against the live episode: `bash …/canon_commit_check.sh c5320329` prints **`ADDS 1 of 96 attachment(s) examined -- c5320329 names bytes it does not contain: ST0057/design.md`** at **rc=1**, and `ADDS 0, rc=0` at the fixed HEAD. It carries the load-bearing adds-only clause, a vacuous-pass arm, and a `--staged` mode built for the hook position. **`int hooks` lists 11 repo-local guards and 4 shipped guards and it is in NEITHER roster. The remaining work is one roster row, not a build.**

**AND THE ORDERING CONSTRAINT IS ALREADY SOLVED, WHICH RETIRES A FINDING OF MINE RATHER THAN ADDING ONE.** I reported that this guard must run AFTER the formatters or it would pass on the only case anyone has produced. **`.githooks/pre-commit:73` already carries that principle verbatim** -- *"DELIBERATELY LAST, after the formatters have re-staged. A gate that runs before the formatter checks content that is not what lands."* `prettier --write` is line 14; `bin/int precommit`'s repo-local guards are line 96. **So it is a constraint to route BY, not one to establish**, and my report was a rediscovery announced as a discovery.

**THE ONE THING THAT IS GENUINELY NEW IS ABOUT THE TOOL'S REMEDY TEXT, NOT ITS DETECTION.** The tool prescribes: *"Sync canon FIRST -- it reads the WORKTREE -- then commit the file(s) and canon together."* **That is exactly the sequence I followed, and it diverged anyway.** Driven: at `c5320329` canon records `db0bd52c` and the file committed in that same commit hashes `abc9a205`, and the byte-level difference is three lines of `*emphasis*` normalised to `_emphasis_` -- **`prettier --write` at `.githooks/pre-commit:14`, rewriting and re-staging the file INSIDE the commit, after canon had hashed it.** There are two markdown writers here and the remedy names neither: an editor-on-save formatter and this hook. **A reader who follows the remedy exactly still lands the defect**, so the detection is complete and the instruction is not. **The tool's guard catches it; the tool's advice does not prevent it.**

**BYTE COUNT STAYED 33538 ACROSS THE WHOLE EPISODE** -- a field still tracking its subject sitting beside one that had stopped, which is why nothing looked wrong at a glance.

**AND THE REWORDING I PROPOSED FOR THAT REMEDY WAS WRONG IN THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION -- cc caught it before either of us handed it to dc (2026-08-20 16:50Z).** I proposed *"sync canon LAST, after the formatters have had the file"*. **It reads naturally as _sync after the commit_, which is precisely what dc's remedy exists to forbid**, and which leaves that commit permanently divergent because a later sync repairs the NEXT commit and can never repair that one. I meant *after you have run the formatter*; a reader following the words lands the worse defect. **A correct finding with a remedy that reads fine and makes it worse -- and I nearly put it in front of the person who would have baked it in.**

**THE UNAMBIGUOUS FORM IS THREE STEPS AND THE ORDER IS THE WHOLE CONTENT: FORMAT, then SYNC, then COMMIT.** Run prettier yourself first; canon then hashes the formatted bytes; the hook's own prettier finds nothing to change and re-stages identical bytes; canon matches what lands. **This works only because prettier is idempotent, so idempotence is load-bearing rather than incidental.**

**DRIVEN TWICE, ON TWO INDEPENDENT PROBES, AND THE DENOMINATOR IS STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED.** cc's probe (emphasis + a ragged table) stabilised in one pass. Mine, authored separately (`*stars*`, `_unders_`, a ragged 3-row table, a `*`-bulleted list): `76d9f4fe` -> `58d68167` -> `58d68167`. **One pass to stabilise, then stable, on both.** **NOT CLAIMED: idempotence over arbitrary markdown.** Two probes carrying the shapes we have actually seen, and nothing wider.

**AND THE PRECONDITION HOLDS FOR THE LIVE FILE RIGHT NOW**, which makes this applicable rather than theoretical: `design.md` at HEAD hashes `abc9a205` and running prettier over a copy of it returns `abc9a205` unchanged. **The estate is currently in the stable state the three-step assumes.**

**IT IS ONE FORMATTER WITH TWO TRIGGER POINTS, NOT TWO FORMATTERS (cc, correcting their own correction).** The same prettier does the emphasis normalisation and the table re-padding; editor-on-save and `.githooks/pre-commit:14` are two triggers for one writer. **The distinction is load-bearing because _two writers_ invites two remedies.**

**NONE OF WHICH CLOSES THIS ROW, AND THE THREE-STEP MUST NOT BE OFFERED AS IF IT DID. An advisory that requires an operator to remember to run a formatter by hand is not a control.** It is a further argument for the roster row: the guard's `--staged` mode is the only form that does not depend on anyone remembering. **The remedy text should be corrected because it is currently followable-and-still-broken, not because correcting it satisfies AC-03.6.** **2026-08-25 -- FILE-ABSENCE NOW SPLITS THREE WAYS, because conflating a missing FILE with missing BYTES made this instrument refuse commits that SATISFY its own criterion.** AC-03.6 states the invariant as _every attachment's recorded bytes are OBTAINABLE from that commit_ and names both sides -- the `text` in canon and the file blob -- and the tool consulted only the blob. **A DEHYDRATED thread (files deliberately removed, canon retaining the bytes) therefore reported ABSENT while fully compliant.** Measured: 54 threads already carry that shape, and `--exhaustive` at HEAD reported **189 of 295 attachments as inherited divergences that were not divergences at all**; after the split it reports 0 of 295, and every one of the 295 was independently confirmed self-consistent (`sha256(text) == recorded sha256`, no exceptions). **The gate never fired on them only because narrowed mode does not examine a thread the commit did not touch -- the first commit to actually dehydrate one was refused.** THE SPLIT: blob present and disagreeing is DIVERGED, untouched (this is `3f10b1ee`, the file running ahead of canon, which dc called the live one); blob absent and the thread DECLARED in `.intentfiles` is ABSENT, untouched (this is `c4f9bcbe`, canon running ahead of the commit); blob absent and NOT declared is dehydrated, and the recorded bytes are verified against canon's own `text`. **CHECKING CANON'S TEXT ALONE WOULD HAVE BEEN A WEAKENING RATHER THAN A FIX** -- canon ingested `c4f9bcbe`'s uncommitted bytes, so its text hashes correctly and it would sail through; the `.intentfiles` arm is the entire difference. **BURNED BEFORE IT WAS TRUSTED:** a realised thread with its blob dropped from the index still reports ADDS and still exits 1. **An unreadable or empty `.intentfiles` counts everything as REALISED**, so history before 2026-08-19 behaves exactly as before and this arm can only over-report.
